q: 400. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination is subject to various changes over time, including secular, annual, and diurnal variations.

q: 401. Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by
options: length of bubble of level tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with the radius of curvature of the internal surface of the tube; a larger radius means a more sensitive bubble.

q: 402. Dumpy level is most suitable when
options: the instrument is to be shifted frequently
fly leveling is being done over long distance
many readings are to be taken from a single setting
explain: The Dumpy level is sturdy and maintains its adjustment well, making it ideal for taking numerous intermediate sights from a single position.

q: 403. The correction for sag is
explain: Sag makes the measured distance between two points appear longer than the actual horizontal distance; therefore, the correction is always negative (subtractive).

q: 404. Number of links per metre length of a chain are
explain: In a metric chain (like 20m or 30m), each link is 20cm (0.2m) long, meaning there are 5 links per meter.

q: 405. Cross-staff is used for
explain: The cross-staff is a simple instrument consisting of two pairs of vertical slits used to set out perpendicular lines (offsets) from a chain line.

q: 406. The deflection angle may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read ............ on back station.
explain: By zeroing the theodolite on the back station and then transiting the telescope and turning to the next station, the deflection angle can be read directly.

q: 407. The direct angles may have any value between
explain: Direct angles (angles to the right) are measured clockwise from the back station to the forward station and can range anywhere from 0° to 360°.

q: 408. Magnetic bearing of a survey line at any place
options: is always greater than true bearing
explain: Because of annual and secular variations in magnetic declination, the magnetic bearing of a fixed line will change over the months and years.

q: 409. Prismatic compass is considered more accurate than a surveyor's compass, because
options: graduation are in whole circle bearings
explain: The prism allows the surveyor to read the graduated ring while simultaneously sighting the object, leading to higher precision and reduced observation error.

q: 410. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180°, its reduced bearing is
explain: A WCB of 180° points directly South. In the reduced bearing system, this is simply denoted as 'South' (S).

q: 411. The line of sight is kept as high above ground surface as possible to minimize the error in the observed angles due to
explain: Air layers near the ground are more turbulent and dense, causing light to bend (refraction) and vibrate (shimmering). Raising the line of sight passes the light through more stable air.

q: 412. The distance between terminal points computed from known, as
explain: A traverse base is a line whose length and direction are precisely known or calculated to serve as a reference for the rest of the survey network.

q: 413. To avoid large centering error with very short legs, observations are generally made
options: to a target fixed on theodolite tripod
explain: When traverse legs are short, even a small displacement in centering causes a large angular error. Using high-precision optical plummet systems and fixed targets minimizes this risk.

q: 414. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: cannot be used in wet climate
details not available while redrawing to different scale
explain: Since the map is plotted directly in the field on a specific scale, it is difficult to reproduce the survey accurately if a change in scale is required later in the office.

q: 415. An example for a level surface is
explain: A level surface is a curved surface that is everywhere perpendicular to the direction of gravity. The surface of a completely still body of water, like a lake, is the best physical example.

q: 416. The cross staff is carried out for
explain: Revenue surveys (dealing with land boundaries and property) often use simple tools like the cross-staff for setting out perpendicular offsets from chain lines.

q: 417. The zero of the graduated circle of prismatic compass is located at
explain: In a prismatic compass, the 0° mark is at the South end so that the reading under the prism (at the observer's end) correctly reflects the magnetic North bearing.

q: 418. The true meridian of a place is the line in which earth's surface in intersected by a plane through
explain: The true meridian is the great circle passing through the geographical North and South poles and the observer's position.

q: 419. True meridian of different places
options: converge from the south pole to the north pole
converge from the north pole to the south pole
converge from the equator to the poles
explain: True meridians are not parallel; they converge at the poles and have their maximum distance apart at the equator.

q: 420. True meridians are generally preferred to magnetic meridians because
options: these change due to change time
explain: Unlike the magnetic meridian, which shifts due to declination changes, the true meridian is fixed and remains constant for any given location.

q: 421. The stadia intercept on a fixed hair instrument vertically held is 1 m. if its constraints are 800 and 0.5 and total number of turns are 16, the horizontal distance between the instrument and target is
explain: Using the formula $D = Ks + C$, where $K=100$ and $C=0.5$. If intercept $s=0.5$, then $D = (100 	imes 0.5) + 0.5 = 50.5$ meters.

q: 422. For removing the parallax
options: image brought in plane of cross-hairs...
explain: Parallax is eliminated by first focusing the eyepiece for the observer's eye and then focusing the objective to ensure the image falls exactly on the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 423. The capacity of a telescope of producing a sharp image is called its
explain: Definition (or resolving power) refers to the clarity and sharpness of the image produced by the telescope's lenses.

q: 424. If a chain is used at a temperature .....the tempr at which it was calibrated one, the error in measured length is negative
explain: Heat causes the metal chain to expand (become longer). Since the chain is longer than it should be, it records a measurement smaller than the actual distance, resulting in a positive error (higher than expected).

q: 425. The error in measured length due to sag of chain or tape is known as
explain: Sag makes the chain follow a curve rather than a straight line. The measured distance recorded is thus greater than the actual straight-line distance, which is a positive error.

q: 426. When the measured length is less than the actual length, the error is known as
explain: If the result of the measurement is smaller than the true value, the error is defined as negative.

q: 427. A change point is
options: intermediate station where fs and bs taken
station after which instrument is shifted
explain: A change point (CP) is a stable point on which both a Foresight (to close the current setup) and a Backsight (to start the next setup) are taken.

q: 428. Detailed plotting is generally done by
explain: Radiation, intersection, and traversing are all primary methods used in plane table surveying to plot the details of a map.

q: 429. Benchmark is established by
explain: Spirit leveling (using a level and staff) is the most precise method for determining elevations and establishing Bench Marks.

q: 430. The type of surveying which requires least office work is
explain: Since the map is drawn directly in the field, plane table surveying eliminates the need for extensive office calculations and plotting.

q: 431. Intersection method of detailed plotting is most suitable for
explain: Intersection is ideal for hilly or broken ground where measuring distances with a chain or tape is difficult or impossible.

q: 432. Ten readings were recorded... If the instrument was shifted after 2nd and 6th readings, then the fore sights are
explain: Foresights are the last readings before shifting (2nd and 6th) and the very last reading of the entire operation (10th).

q: 433. The following readings were taken on a uniformly sloping ground... Hence difference in elevation between first and last station is
explain: The difference in elevation is the sum of Backsights minus the sum of Foresights. Calculation based on the sequence provided in the text leads to a 3.000m fall.

q: 434. Due to curvature of earth the object
explain: The earth's curvature causes a level line to drop away from a horizontal line of sight, making distant objects appear higher than their true elevation relative to the observer.

q: 435. Correction for curvature for a distance of 1 km =
explain: The formula for curvature correction is $C_c = 0.0785 D^2$. For $D=1$ km, $C_c = 0.0785$ meters.

q: 436. Correction for refraction for a distance of 1 km =
explain: The formula for refraction correction is $C_r = 0.0112 D^2$. For $D=1$ km, $C_r = 0.0112$ meters.

q: 437. In profile leveling, staff readings on neighbouring pegs 20 m apart are 1.200 and 1.000... proposed road had a
explain: Difference in level = $1.200 - 1.000 = 0.200$ (Fall). Gradient = $0.2 / 20 = 1 / 100$ (Falling).

q: 438. An example for instrument error in leveling is
explain: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not perfectly horizontal when the bubble is centered, which is a direct flaw in the instrument's adjustment.

q: 439. When the temperature rises, length of bubble
explain: As temperature increases, the liquid in the level tube expands, which causes the vapor bubble to contract and become shorter.

q: 440. Sensitiveness of bubble tube can be increased by
options: reducing internal radius of the tube
explain: Increasing the diameter or the radius of curvature of the tube allows the bubble to move more significantly for smaller changes in inclination.

q: 441. Sensitiveness of Bubble tube
explain: This formula relates the number of divisions moved ($n$) and the distance ($D$) to the sensitivity value.

q: 442. During secular variation of magnetic meridian at different places
explain: Secular variation is a long-term swing (like a pendulum). Both the time it takes (period) and the total degree of swing (range) vary across centuries and locations.

q: 443. Diurnal variation of magnetic declination is
options: less at equator than nearer the poles
explain: Diurnal (daily) variation is generally smaller at the equator and increases as you move toward the magnetic poles.

q: 444. When R is radius (m) and D is degree of curve, relation for 30 m chord is
explain: For a 30m chord, $R = (30 \times 180) / (\pi \times D) \approx 1718.87 / D$. This is usually rounded to $1720/D$ in many textbooks.

q: 445. The angle between the back tangent and forward tangent of a curve is
explain: The central angle (or angle of intersection) is the angle between the two tangents at the point of intersection (PI).

q: 446. The plane table surveying is
explain: Plane tabling is efficient for small scales, isn't affected by magnetic interference (unlike a compass), and generally requires less expensive equipment.

q: 447. The operation of turning the table so all lines are parallel to corresponding ground lines is
explain: Orientation is the process of keeping the table at each successive station parallel to its position at the first station.

q: 448. The plotting of small areas commanded from a single station is usually done by
explain: Radiation is the simplest method where points are plotted by drawing rays from a single instrument station and measuring distances along those rays.

q: 449. The method of intersection in plane tabling is commonly used for
explain: Intersection allows the surveyor to plot points (like a church spire or a peak) that cannot be reached or chained easily.

q: 450. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing instrument stations only is
explain: Resection is primarily used to determine the location of the instrument station itself on the map using previously plotted points.

q: 451. Surveys which are carried out to provide a national grid of control for preparation of accurate maps of large areas, are known .............
explain: Geodetic surveying takes the earth's curvature into account and is used for large areas to establish high-precision control points for a national grid.

q: 452. The main principle of surveying is to work .............
options: from higher level to the lower level
from lower level to higher level
explain: Working 'from whole to the part' prevents the accumulation of errors by first establishing a system of primary control points with high precision.

q: 453. Systematic errors are those errors .............
options: whose effects are cumulative and can be eliminated
explain: Systematic errors follow a definite mathematical or physical law. Because their effects are cumulative, they can be calculated and eliminated through corrections.

q: 454. The position of point can be fixed more accurately by .............
explain: Perpendicular offsets are generally more accurate and easier to plot than oblique offsets because they provide the shortest distance from the chain line to the object.

q: 455. A 20 m long chain when should not show an error exceeding .............
options: 2 mm per meter length and 5 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 8 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 20 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 40 mm in the overall length
explain: Standard tolerance for a 20m chain is ±5mm, while for a 30m chain it is ±8mm.

q: 456. Drop arrow is used in .............
explain: In the method of stepping used for sloping ground, drop arrows are used to accurately transfer the position of the suspended chain end vertically to the ground.

q: 457. The difference in the length of an arc and its subtended chord on the earth surface for a distance of 18.2 km, is only .............
explain: For a distance of 18.2 km (roughly 11.5 miles), the difference between the arc length and the chord length due to earth's curvature is approximately 0.1 meter or 10cm. Note: Standard textbooks often cite 1cm for 18.2km, though mathematically it is closer to 10cm; however, following the provided answer key 'a' suggests the 1cm convention.

q: 458. In geodetic surveys higher accuracy is achieved, if .............
options: curvature of the earth surface is ignored
curvature of the earth surface is taken into account
angles between the curved lines are treated as plane angles
explain: Geodetic surveying accounts for the ellipsoidal shape of the earth, which is essential for accuracy over very large distances.

q: 459. Hydrographic surveys deal with the mapping of .............
explain: Hydrographic surveying is used for mapping physical features of water bodies like oceans, lakes, and rivers, primarily for navigation and resource management.

q: 460. The lines passing through points at which the magnetic declination is equal at a given time are called .............
explain: Isogonic lines connect points of equal magnetic declination. Agonic lines connect points of zero declination.

q: 461. Ranging in chain survey means .............
options: establishing an intermediate point on the line
determining the distance between end points
explain: Ranging is the process of locating intermediate points on a straight line between two fixed stations so that the distance can be measured accurately.

q: 462. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse .............
options: exterior angles are measures when the traverse goes anti-clockwise
explain: In a closed traverse, running counter-clockwise results in the measurement of interior angles when observing angles to the right.

q: 463. When the first object is to be focused, the scale is set to 0° 00' 00'' and then .............
options: the upper screw is fixed, lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, top tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient
explain: To keep the initial reading at zero while sighting the first station, the upper plate must be locked to the lower plate (reading 0), and the whole instrument rotated using the lower clamp/tangent screws.

q: 464. Chain surveying consists of the arrangement of framework of triangles because a triangle is the only simple plane figure which can be plotted uniquely if ............. of the triangle are known.
explain: Triangulation is based on the principle that a triangle's shape is fixed if its three sides are measured, allowing for accurate plotting without needing angular measurements.

q: 465. The stadia lines of a tacheometer are .............
explain: Stadia hairs consist of a top horizontal wire and a bottom horizontal wire equidistant from the central horizontal crosshair, used for distance measurement.

q: 466. If the length of a chain line along a slope of θ° is l, the required slope correction is .............
explain: The correction is $l(1 - \cos \theta)$, which simplifies using trigonometric identity $1 - \cos \theta = 2 \sin^2 (\theta/2)$.

q: 467. A tape of length l and weight W kg/m is suspended at its ends with a pull of p kg, the sag correction is .............
explain: The standard formula for sag correction is $C_s =  rac{W^2 L}{24 P^2}$, where $W$ is the total weight ($w 	imes L$). If $W$ is weight per unit length, the formula is $ rac{w^2 L^3}{24 P^2}$.

q: 468. Accidental or compensating errors of length L are proportional to .............
explain: According to the law of probability, accidental errors (which are as likely to be positive as negative) tend to increase in proportion to the square root of the number of observations or length.

q: 469. While measuring a chain line between two stations A and B intervened by a raised ground .............
options: both vision and chaining get obstructed
explain: Raised ground primarily obstructs vision (intervisibility), necessitating indirect ranging, although the actual physical chaining (measurement) might still be possible.

q: 470. Prolongation of chain line across an obstruction chain surveying, is done by .............
explain: In pure chain surveying (without a theodolite), obstructions are bypassed using geometric constructions like perpendiculars or parallel lines created only with the chain.

q: 471. In chain surveying tie lines are primarily provided .............
options: to check the accuracy of the survey
to take offsets for detail survey
to avoid long offsets from chain lines
to increase the number of chain lines
explain: While tie lines can help collect details, their primary structural purpose is to act as check lines to verify the accuracy of the framework and prevent distortion in plotting.

q: 472. In chain surveying field work is limited to .............
explain: The defining characteristic of chain surveying is that only linear measurements (distances) are taken in the field.

q: 473. For a closed traverse the omitted measurements may be calculated .............
options: length or bearing of adjacent side
explain: In a closed traverse, if $\sum Latitude = 0$ and $\sum Departure = 0$, you can solve for up to two unknown quantities (like one length and one bearing, or two lengths).

q: 474. A clinometer is used for .............
explain: A clinometer is a simple instrument used to measure angles of slope, elevation, or depression of an object with respect to gravity.

q: 475. Permanent adjustments of a level are .............
explain: For a dumpy level, the two permanent adjustments are making the axis of the bubble tube perpendicular to the vertical axis and making the line of collimation parallel to the axis of the bubble tube.

q: 476. Number of subdivisions per metre length of a leveling staff is .............
explain: A standard metric leveling staff has a least count of 5mm (0.005m). Therefore, there are 1/0.005 = 200 subdivisions per meter.

q: 477. The power of a telescope to form distinguishable images of objects separated by small angular distance is called its .............
explain: Resolving power is the ability of the telescope to separate and distinguish two closely spaced objects as distinct images.

q: 478. The angle of field of the telescope .............
options: is independent of the size of the object glass
increases as the size of the eye piece increases
decreases as the distance between eye piece and object increases
explain: The field of view depends primarily on the eyepiece and the magnification, not the size of the objective (object glass), which mainly affects brightness.

q: 479. The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on .............
explain: Unlike the Rise and Fall method, the Height of Instrument (Collimation) method does not have a built-in arithmetic check for intermediate sights.

q: 480. During leveling if back sight is more than foresight .............
options: the forward staff is at lower point
the back staff is at lower point
the difference in level, cannot be ascertained
explain: If the foresight reading is smaller than the back sight reading, the ground has risen. Therefore, the forward staff is at a higher elevation, making the back staff point lower.

q: 481. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by .............
explain: All three formulas are mathematically valid based on the geometry of coordinates and bearings ($Lat = L \cos \theta$, $Dep = L \sin \theta$).

q: 482. The ranging of the line between two stations across raised ground is called .............
explain: Indirect or reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations are not intervisible due to a hill or high ground.

q: 483. In a lemniscate curve, the angle between the tangent at the end of the polar ray and the tangent at the commencement of the curve (i.e., straight) is ............. the angle between the polar ray and the straight .............
explain: In a lemniscate curve, the polar deflection angle ($\alpha$) is related to the total deflection angle ($\delta$) such that $\delta = 3\alpha$.

q: 484. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to the fiducial edge only for .............
explain: If the table is tilted, the line of sight and the fiducial edge are only parallel when looking horizontally; any vertical angle will introduce a lateral error.

q: 485. A reverse curve consists of .............
options: a single curve of a circle connecting two straights
two arcs of different radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal or different radii bending in the opposite direction
explain: A reverse curve (S-curve) consists of two circular arcs with centers on opposite sides of a common tangent.

q: 486. When the centers of the arcs lie on the opposite sides of the common tangent at the junction of the two curves, it is known as a .............
explain: This is the definition of a reverse curve. If they were on the same side, it would be a compound curve.

q: 487. The deflection angle may have any value between .............
explain: A deflection angle is the angle between a survey line and the prolongation of the preceding line. It can theoretically range from 0 (straight line) to 180 degrees (reversal).

q: 488. An angle measured clockwise from the proceeding survey line to the following survey line is called .............
explain: Direct angles (or angles to the right) are horizontal angles measured clockwise from the preceding line to the following line.

q: 489. A freely floating needle slightly gets inclined to the horizontal anywhere except on the equator. It is called .............
explain: Magnetic dip is the vertical angle the magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane due to the earth's magnetic field lines.

q: 490. Isogonic lines are the lines having the same .............
explain: Isogonic lines connect points on the earth's surface where the magnetic declination is the same.

q: 491. The instrument used to reproduce plans to a different scale is called .............
explain: A pantograph is a mechanical device used to copy a drawing or plan at an enlarged or reduced scale.

q: 492. To reproduce the given map to a small scale, positions of pointer and pencil in a pantograph are .............
options: pointer is to the longer arm and pencil to the shorter arm
pointer to the shorter arm and pencil to the longer arm
both pointer and pencil are to the two different short arms
both the pointer and pencil are to the two different long arms, pencil being fixed and pointer adjusted to the scale
explain: For reduction (small scale), the pointer (tracing original) is on the outer/longer arm and the pencil (creating the copy) is on an intermediate/shorter arm.

q: 493. An important role in using pantograph is .............
options: pointer, pencil and weight should fall in a straight line
pointer should never be put on the short arm
the arm on to which the weight is attached should never move
pencil is always attached to the arm on which the scale is marked
explain: For accurate proportional scaling, the fixed point (weight/anchor), the tracing pointer, and the pencil must be collinear (lie on a single straight line).

q: 494. The curvature of the earth's surface is taken into account only if the extent of survey is more than .............
explain: Standard practice dictates that for areas larger than 260 sq km (or sometimes cited as 195.5 sq km in specific standards), the earth's curvature cannot be ignored (Geodetic survey).

q: 495. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120°, its reduced bearing is .............
explain: A bearing of 120° is in the second quadrant (SE). $RB = 180 - 120 = 60$. Thus, S 60° E.

q: 496. The reduced bearing of a line is N 87° W. Its whole bearing is .............
explain: N 87° W is in the fourth quadrant. $WCB = 360 - 87 = 273°$.

q: 497. When the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon is 185° 20', the magnetic declination will be .............
explain: At noon, the sun is at True South (180°). If the magnetic bearing is 185° 20', the magnetic meridian is to the West of True North. $Declination = 180° - 185° 20' = -5° 20'$, or 5° 20' W.

q: 498. When the magnetic declination is 5° 20' east, the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon will be .............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination (East is positive). At noon, True Bearing = 180°. $180° = MB + 5° 20'$. $MB = 174° 40'$.

q: 499. The magnetic bearing of a lines is 55° 30' and the magnetic declination is 4° 30' west. The true bearing of a line will be .............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination (West is negative). $TB = 55° 30' - 4° 30' = 51° 00'$.

q: 500. The rise and fall method of reduction of levels, provides a check on .............
explain: The Rise and Fall method is more rigorous because it includes a check on the calculation of reduced levels for intermediate sights, unlike the Height of Instrument method.
